subject.title: feat: keep reset session history searchable

question: Should OpenClaw adopt searchable retained generations after session reset as the core default once the identified cleanup and reporting defects are repaired?
rationale: This is a deliberate persistent-session retention and storage-policy change, not a narrow correction to an established public behavior; maintainers must decide whether the new reset semantics belong in core.

options.title: Keep draft and finish the retention design
options.body: Repair the four identified lifecycle and budget defects, add upgrade-focused proof, then review the retained-history behavior as the intended core default.

options.title: Narrow to existing reset semantics
options.body: Drop retained SQLite generations and limit the branch to any independently safe accounting or documentation correction.

options.title: Defer the feature direction
options.body: Close or pause the branch if maintainers do not want reset history retention to change in the current session model.

recommendation.title: Keep draft and finish the retention design
recommendation.body: Repair the four identified lifecycle and budget defects, add upgrade-focused proof, then review the retained-history behavior as the intended core default.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation and stated retention design originate from this contributor, who is the best available routing point for the concrete technical follow-up; final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
